36533: Egyptian servant who bears Ishmael and names God "Thou God seest me".
36535: Looks back toward Sodom and becomes a pillar of salt; Jesus says "Remember Lot's wife".
36536: Chosen for Isaac at the well; helps Jacob gain the blessing.
36537: Jacob's first wife, mother of Levi and Judah.
36538: Jacob's beloved wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin; Jeremiah pictures her weeping for her children.
36539: Jacob's daughter, violated at Shechem; her brothers take revenge.
36541: Secures her right to an heir by disguise; ancestor of David and Jesus.
36543: Hebrew midwives who fear God and defy Pharaoh's order to kill newborn boys.
36545: Mother of Moses, Aaron and Miriam; hides the infant Moses.
36548: Prophetess who leads Israel's women in song at the sea.
36549: Midianite wife of Moses who circumcises their son.
36550: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah petition Moses and win the right to inherit.
36551: Canaanite of Jericho who hides the spies; commended for faith and works.
36553: Caleb's daughter who asks her father for springs of water.
36554: Prophetess and judge; leads Israel against Sisera.
36555: Kills Sisera with a tent peg; "blessed above women".
36557: Meets her father with timbrels and becomes the victim of his vow; mourned yearly.
36559: Wife of Manoah, visited by the angel and told to keep the Nazirite rule.
36560: Betrays Samson to the Philistines for silver.
36561: Bereaved widow who returns from Moab and guides Ruth.
36562: Moabite who pledges loyalty to Naomi and Naomi's God; great-grandmother of David.
36563: Ruth's sister-in-law who returns to her people.
36564: Prays for a son, dedicates Samuel and sings a song of reversal.
36566: Saul's daughter and David's wife; saves his life and later despises him.
36567: Wise wife of Nabal who averts David's vengeance; later David's wife.
36569: Consulted by Saul to bring up Samuel.
36570: Taken by David; mother of Solomon and queen mother.
36572: Raped by her half-brother Amnon; avenged by Absalom.
36574: Recruited by Joab to persuade David to bring Absalom home.
36575: Saul's concubine who guards her sons' bodies from the birds.
36577: Tests Solomon's wisdom; Jesus says she will rise in the judgment.
36578: Sidonian queen of Ahab who promotes Baal and arranges Naboth's murder.
36579: Feeds Elijah in famine; her son is raised.
36580: Hosts Elisha; her son is promised, dies and is raised.
36582: Captive Israelite girl who points her master to the prophet in Samaria.
36583: Queen mother who seizes Judah's throne for six years.
36585: King Jehoram's daughter who hides the infant Joash.
36586: Prophetess consulted on the book of the law.
36588: Hosea's wife, whose unfaithfulness becomes a prophetic sign.
36589: Persian queen deposed for refusing to appear at the king's feast.
36591: Jewish queen of Persia who risks her life to save her people.
36592: Virgin of Nazareth who conceives by the Holy Spirit; present at the cross and in the upper room.
36594: Mother of John the Baptist; filled with the Spirit, she blesses Mary.
36595: Aged prophetess in the temple who speaks of the child Jesus.
36596: Healed disciple and patron; first witness of the resurrection. Western tradition from Gregory the Great conflated her with the sinful woman of Luke 7; the text does not.
36597: Wife of Herod's steward Chuza; supports Jesus and witnesses the empty tomb.
36598: One of the women who provide for Jesus from their means.
36600: Watches the crucifixion and brings spices to the tomb; often identified with the mother of Zebedee's sons.
36602: Stands by the cross with Jesus' mother.
36604: Hosts Jesus at Bethany and confesses him as the Christ.
36605: Sits at Jesus' feet and anoints him for burial.
36607: Converses with Jesus at Jacob's well and brings her town to him.
36608: The woman with the issue of blood
36609: Healed after twelve years by touching Jesus' garment.
36610: A Gentile whose persistent answer wins healing for her daughter.
36613: The woman who anointed Jesus in Galilee
36614: A "sinner" who washes Jesus' feet with tears in a Pharisee's house.
36615: Wife of Antipas who demands John the Baptist's head.
36616: Lies with Ananias about the price of their land and dies.
36619: Disciple at Joppa full of good works; raised by Peter.

36622: Servant girl who is so glad to hear Peter that she forgets to open the door.

36625: Believes after Paul's speech at the Areopagus.
36627: Tentmaker and teacher who with Aquila instructs Apollos; often named before her husband.
36630: Servant (deacon) of the church at Cenchreae and patron of Paul, likely the bearer of Romans.
36632: Women who laboured with Paul in the gospel, urged to agree in the Lord.

36638: For each book: the traditional attribution (from the text itself, Jewish tradition such as the Talmud's *Baba Bathra* 14b-15a, or early church writers) and the main lines of modern critical scholarship. Many books are anonymous; "traditional" and "scholarly" here are descriptions of views, not verdicts. Conservative scholars defend many traditional attributions with arguments of their own.
36639: Traditional: Moses. Scholarly: a composite of sources or layers (the Documentary Hypothesis's J, E, P, or newer supplementary and fragmentary models), reaching final form in the exilic or Persian period.
36641: Traditional: Moses, who is said to write down God's words. Scholarly: composite, as for Genesis.
36642: Traditional: Moses. Scholarly: largely the Priestly source and Holiness Code, often dated exilic or post-exilic, though some argue for older material.
36643: Traditional: Moses, who records the stages of the journey. Scholarly: composite with priestly and non-priestly strands.
36644: Traditional: Moses (with the account of his death by Joshua or a later hand). Scholarly: core law code linked to Josiah's reform (7th century BC), framed later.
36645: Traditional: Joshua (Talmud), who "wrote these words in the book of the law of God". Scholarly: part of the Deuteronomistic History, compiled in the late monarchy and exile.
36647: Traditional: Samuel (Talmud). Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History, using older hero stories and the Song of Deborah, one of the oldest poems in the Bible.
36648: Traditional: Samuel (Talmud). Scholarly: anonymous; dated to the monarchy by some and to the post-exilic period by others.
36649: Traditional: Samuel, with Nathan and Gad completing it (based on 1 Chr 29:29). Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History drawing on earlier narratives such as the ark story and David's rise.
36650: Traditional: Nathan and Gad. Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History incorporating the so-called Succession Narrative (2 Sam 9-20; 1 Kgs 1-2).
36651: Traditional: Jeremiah (Talmud). Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History, citing sources such as the acts of Solomon and the chronicles of the kings.
36652: Traditional: Jeremiah. Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History, finished after 561 BC since it records Jehoiachin's release.
36653: Traditional: Ezra (Talmud). Scholarly: "the Chronicler", a Levitical author of the late Persian period (c. 400-350 BC), probably distinct from Ezra-Nehemiah.
36654: Traditional: Ezra. Scholarly: the Chronicler, as above.
36655: Traditional: Ezra, with first-person memoirs. Scholarly: Ezra-Nehemiah (one book in the Hebrew Bible) compiled from Ezra and Nehemiah memoirs and Persian documents.
36656: Traditional: Nehemiah ("the words of Nehemiah"). Scholarly: Nehemiah memoir embedded in Ezra-Nehemiah.
36657: Traditional: Mordecai or the Men of the Great Assembly. Scholarly: anonymous, late Persian or early Hellenistic period.
36658: Traditional: the Talmud names Moses; others suggest Job himself or Solomon. Scholarly: anonymous, usually dated 6th-4th century BC, with debate over the unity of the speeches of Elihu.
36660: Traditional: David and others named in superscriptions (Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses, Heman, Ethan). Scholarly: a collection formed over centuries; the superscriptions are generally seen as later editorial notes.
36661: Traditional: Solomon, with sections by "the wise", Agur and Lemuel, and proverbs copied by Hezekiah's men. Scholarly: a collection of collections, some possibly monarchic, finalised after the exile.
36662: Traditional: Solomon, "the Preacher, the son of David". Scholarly: a later sage writing in Solomon's persona, often dated 3rd century BC on linguistic grounds.
36664: Traditional: Solomon. Scholarly: anonymous love poetry, possibly an anthology; the superscription may mean "for" or "about" Solomon.
36665: Traditional: Isaiah son of Amoz; the NT quotes both halves under his name. Scholarly: First Isaiah (1-39, 8th century), Second Isaiah (40-55, exilic) and Third Isaiah (56-66, post-exilic).
36667: Traditional: Jeremiah, dictating to Baruch. Scholarly: Jeremiah's oracles with Baruch's narratives and Deuteronomistic prose; the Greek text is about one-eighth shorter.
36668: Traditional: Jeremiah (Greek preface and Talmud). Scholarly: anonymous poems composed soon after 586 BC, perhaps by several authors.
36669: Traditional: Ezekiel the priest. Scholarly: broadly accepted as substantially from Ezekiel, with some editorial expansion by his circle.
36670: Traditional: Daniel in the 6th century BC; Jesus refers to "Daniel the prophet". Scholarly: court tales (1-6) earlier, with the visions (7-12) completed c. 167-164 BC during the Maccabean crisis; conservatives defend a 6th-century date.
36671: Traditional: Hosea son of Beeri. Scholarly: mainly Hosea, with Judean editing after Samaria's fall.
36673: Traditional: Joel son of Pethuel. Scholarly: authorship accepted; date disputed from pre-exilic to Persian period.
36674: Traditional: Amos of Tekoa. Scholarly: mainly Amos; the hopeful ending (9:11-15) is often attributed to a later hand.
36675: Traditional: Obadiah, sometimes identified (Talmud) with Ahab's steward. Scholarly: anonymous prophet after 586 BC.
36676: Traditional: Jonah son of Amittai. Scholarly: anonymous third-person narrative about the 8th-century prophet, usually dated post-exilic.
36677: Traditional: Micah of Moresheth. Scholarly: chapters 1-3 widely accepted; parts of 4-7 often dated later.
36678: Traditional: Nahum the Elkoshite. Scholarly: accepted; written between 663 and 612 BC.
36679: Traditional: Habakkuk the prophet. Scholarly: accepted; late 7th century BC; the psalm of chapter 3 may have circulated separately.
36680: Traditional: Zephaniah. Scholarly: accepted, with some later additions in the closing promises.
36681: Traditional: Haggai. Scholarly: Haggai's oracles in a third-person editorial frame, 520 BC.
36682: Traditional: Zechariah son of Berechiah. Scholarly: chapters 1-8 from Zechariah (520-518 BC); chapters 9-14 ("Deutero-Zechariah") from later hands.
36683: Traditional: Malachi. Scholarly: possibly anonymous ("my messenger" as a title), mid-5th century BC.
36684: Traditional: the apostle Matthew (Papias, Irenaeus). Scholarly: anonymous Jewish-Christian author c. AD 80-90 who used Mark; minority defend Matthean authorship.
36686: Traditional: John Mark, recording Peter's preaching (Papias). Scholarly: generally the earliest Gospel, c. AD 65-70; the link to Peter is debated but the name Mark is widely accepted.
36687: Traditional: Luke the physician, Paul's companion. Scholarly: same author as Acts; Lukan authorship debated but widely held possible; c. AD 80-90 (some date earlier).
36688: Traditional: John son of Zebedee, the beloved disciple. Scholarly: the beloved disciple tradition shaped by a Johannine community, c. AD 90-100; identity of the beloved disciple debated.
36689: Traditional: Luke; the "we" passages suggest an eyewitness companion of Paul. Scholarly: same author as Luke; whether the "we" sections reflect the author's presence is debated.
36690: Paul (undisputed), written down by Tertius from Corinth c. AD 57.
36692: Paul (undisputed), with Sosthenes, from Ephesus c. AD 54-55.
36693: Paul (undisputed), with Timothy; many scholars see a compilation of several letters.
36694: Paul (undisputed); date and destination (north vs south Galatia) debated.
36695: Traditional: Paul from prison. Scholarly: widely regarded as deutero-Pauline (style, theology, dependence on Colossians); defended as Pauline by many conservatives.
36696: Paul (undisputed), with Timothy, from prison (Rome, Ephesus or Caesarea).
36697: Traditional: Paul with Timothy. Scholarly: disputed; roughly evenly divided between Pauline and deutero-Pauline.
36698: Paul (undisputed) with Silvanus and Timothy, c. AD 50; probably the earliest NT writing.
36699: Traditional: Paul. Scholarly: disputed because of its eschatology and close literary dependence on 1 Thessalonians.
36700: Traditional: Paul. Scholarly: the Pastoral Epistles are widely judged pseudonymous (c. AD 100) on grounds of vocabulary and church order; defended as Pauline, perhaps via a secretary, by others.
36701: Traditional: Paul's last letter from Roman imprisonment. Scholarly: Pastoral, as above; some see genuine Pauline fragments.
36702: Traditional: Paul. Scholarly: Pastoral, as above.
36704: Anonymous. Eastern tradition credited Paul (Clement of Alexandria and Origen with reservations; Origen said only God knows); Tertullian named Barnabas, Luther suggested Apollos, Harnack proposed Priscilla. Modern scholarship regards it as non-Pauline.
36706: Traditional: James the Lord's brother. Scholarly: debated; some see a pseudonymous work in polished Greek, others defend James (perhaps with help), c. AD 45-62.
36707: Traditional: Peter, "by Silvanus". Scholarly: debated; many judge it pseudonymous (c. AD 80-90) because of its Greek and setting; others accept Peter with Silvanus as secretary.
36708: Traditional: Peter, claiming to be an eyewitness of the transfiguration. Scholarly: widely regarded as pseudonymous (early 2nd century), using Jude; it was among the disputed books in the early church.
36709: Traditional: John the apostle. Scholarly: anonymous; same circle as the Fourth Gospel.
36710: Traditional: John the apostle. Scholarly: "the elder", perhaps the John the Elder mentioned by Papias.
36711: Traditional: John the apostle. Scholarly: "the elder", as for 2 John.
36712: Traditional: Jude, brother of James (and of Jesus). Scholarly: debated; some see a pseudonymous work, others accept the brother of Jesus.
36713: Traditional: John the apostle (Justin Martyr, Irenaeus). Scholarly: a prophet named John on Patmos; Dionysius of Alexandria already argued on stylistic grounds that he was not the evangelist. Usually dated c. AD 95 under Domitian.
36716: Scripture names only two angels: Michael and Gabriel. Other heavenly beings appear as categories (seraphim, cherubim, living creatures) or by function (the angel of the LORD, destroying angel, watchers). Fallen beings are included for completeness. Raphael and Uriel belong to deuterocanonical and later Jewish literature, not the Protestant canon.
36718: Called "one of the chief princes" and "the archangel"; protector of Israel who disputes with the devil over Moses' body and wars against the dragon.
36721: Explains Daniel's visions and announces the births of John and Jesus; "that stand in the presence of God".
36723: Appears only in Tobit (deuterocanonical: canonical for Catholic and Orthodox churches, apocryphal for Protestants), where he calls himself one of seven holy angels before God. Revelation's "seven angels which stood before God" are often compared.
36726: Six-winged beings above the throne crying "Holy, holy, holy"; one touches Isaiah's lips with a coal. The name likely relates to "burning".
36729: Guard Eden's way, are depicted in gold on the mercy seat, and bear the throne-chariot in Ezekiel.
36731: Four creatures with faces of man, lion, ox and eagle in Ezekiel, identified by him as cherubim; Revelation's four creatures worship before the throne.
36733: The title appears twice: of Michael and of the archangel's voice at Christ's return. Later tradition lists seven.
36735: "A watcher and an holy one" decrees Nebuchadnezzar's humbling; the term was developed in *1 Enoch*.
36737: Speaks as God and is addressed as God (Hagar, Moses at the bush, Gideon). Many church fathers and Reformed interpreters see a pre-incarnate appearance of the Son; others see a created angel bearing God's name, as in much Jewish interpretation.
36740: Appears to Joshua near Jericho and tells him to remove his shoes, for the place is holy.
36742: Strikes Israel after David's census and the Assyrian camp in Hezekiah's day.
36744: Jesus says the little ones' angels always behold the Father's face; Hebrews calls angels ministering spirits for the heirs of salvation.
36746: One or two angels announce the resurrection to the women.
36748: Appears to Jesus in Gethsemane (the verse is absent from some early manuscripts).
36750: Each letter in Revelation is addressed to "the angel" of a church; interpreted as guardian angels, as the churches' messengers or leaders, or as personifications of each church.
36752: The adversary in the heavenly court of Job and Zechariah; in the NT the devil, deceiver and tempter.
36755: "Destroyer", the angel of the bottomless pit and king over the locusts.
36757: Called "the prince of the devils" by Jesus' opponents; Jesus links him with Satan.
36759: The KJV renders "day star" in a taunt against the king of Babylon as Lucifer. Many church fathers applied it to Satan's fall; most modern commentators read it primarily of the human king.
36761: Their union with "the daughters of men" is read as fallen angels (early Jewish and patristic view, cf. 1 Pet 3:19-20; Jude 1:6), as the line of Seth, or as royal tyrants.
